issue_context.title: SequenceReader<T>.Rewind(0) causes TryRead() to throw IndexOutOfRangeException
issue_context.body:
### Description

If `SequenceReader<T>.Rewind(0)` is called, any subsequent calls to `TryRead()` will throw IndexOutOfRange exception, as Rewind sets `_moreData` to false without checking if it actually rewound.

### Reproduction Steps

Here's a minimal program which exhibits the bug:
```cs
using System;
using System.Buffers;
using System.IO.Pipelines;
using System.Text;

var pipe = new Pipe();

pipe.Writer.Write(Encoding.UTF8.GetBytes("hello world"));
pipe.Writer.FlushAsync().AsTask().GetAwaiter().GetResult();
pipe.Writer.Complete();

if (!pipe.Reader.TryRead(out var result))
    Console.WriteLine("Read failed");

var reader = new SequenceReader<byte>(result.Buffer);

while (true)
{
    if (!reader.TryRead(out byte x))
        break;

    var offset = reader.Sequence.GetOffset(reader.Position);
    Console.WriteLine($"Success (ofs={offset}, x={(x == 10 ? "\\n" : (char)x)})");

    reader.Rewind(0); // cause bug
}
```

### Expected behavior

`Rewind(0)` should either fail (ArgumentOutOfRangeException?) or it should not set `_moreData` to false.

### Actual behavior

The SequenceReader's `_moreData` field gets set to `false`, meaning that a subsequent `TryRead` does an out-of-bounds read on `CurrentSpan`, throwing an IndexOutOfRangeException.

### Regression?

This seems to have been an issue as far back as 3.1.23, at least going through the runtimes I have installed

### Known Workarounds

Check that the amount to rewind is greater than zero before calling `Rewind`

### Configuration

The project is targeting `net6.0`.
